draft.text: You came in because you had chest pain that was very worrying.
You also mentioned swelling in your right leg that doesn't go away when you rest.
You told us you had a heart attack recently and needed a stent.
You also said you have a lower heart pumping strength, called ejection fraction, which is now 35%.
There is also some moderate mitral regurgitation, which means your heart valve isn't closing properly.
Your chest pain and leg swelling might be related to your heart condition.
You were told about these issues before, but you didn't get detailed results from your angiogram or recent tests.
You will need to keep taking your medicines as prescribed.
We will check on you to see if your condition changes.

unverified_summary.text: You came in because you had chest pain two weeks ago that was very strong and didn't get better with rest.
You also mentioned swelling in your right leg that doesn't go away when you rest.
We didn't do any tests or check your body measurements during this visit.
Your chest pain and leg swelling might be related to your heart condition, including your recent heart attack and stent placement.
You will need to talk to your primary care doctor about your recent echocardiogram and blood test results.
You should keep taking your medicines as prescribed.
A cardiologist will be contacted to help manage your heart condition.
